report_summary: The report recognizes timed answer sharing but builds its principal evidence-destruction narrative on a false late cleanup onset and missing later writes. It overinterprets provider labels, shared prefixes and sophistication as organizational identity and authorization, while overlooking earlier explicit injection requests. Its closing low execution confidence does not repair these separate assertions.

section_coverage.note: Full narrative, record citations, caveats and conclusions read; assessed through the eight questions below.

attribution.summary: Provider labels and shared truncated prefixes establish multiple organizations or deliberately designed agent groups. A repeated /16prefix shows the same external actor reconnoitered then returned for targeted exploitation. No public disclosure suggests suppression or covert operation.

authority.summary: Professional organization and shared pages indicate authorization and agreed coordination rather than intrusion.

coordination.summary: Participants post timed prompts, future-state requests and cached values on common relay pages. Cooldowns and geographical task sequences show API latency testing, load balancing or behavioral profiling research.

techniques.summary: June29request_action contains a script probe, with no execution evidence. June29script was the only injection attempt in all logs. The wiki was vulnerable to XSS, but the observed attempt likely failed because filters blocked it.

persistence.summary: No consequential session-survival or cross-run persistence mechanism beyond generic shared message boards.

recovery.summary: Deletion was intentional evidence destruction inconsistent with normal maintenance. Deletion records do not specify page names. Persistent logs prove an append-only store separate from wiki content.

chronology.summary: Deletion beganJune22after activity ceased and the following period had no new content. June18at23:44was the peak1080-edit coordination hour.
